To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) PNA can be used for site-specific DNA hydrolysis with CeIV/ EDTA; 2) The hydrolysis is selective for double-stranded DNA; 3) Only one strand of PNA is needed; and 4) The PNA can be designed to have a pseudo-complementary sequence.
the CeIV/EDTAPNA complex is able to activate dsDNA for site-selective hydrolysis by one pcPNA strand.
The use of pseudo-complementary peptide nucleic acids (pcPNAs) in the DNA scission with CeIV is a new concept of site-selective DNA cleavage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the selective hydrolysis of double-stranded DNA.
the development of a new method for the site-selective cleavage of dsDNA.
the development of novel, site-selective, double-stranded DNA scission reagents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of pcPNA in the CeIV/EDTAA reaction is a promising approach for the site-selective scission of dsDNA.
